answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a copper-backed stake that only unlocks after a vesting period: creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital up front, and the stake is slashed when an identity is caught attesting for itself. Like shale layers that only form under sustained pressure over time, trust accrues slowly, so a violet burst of fresh identities cannot instantly outvote established agents. Attackers must pay the bond for every fake, making a swarm far more expensive than the influence it buys.
